column1: The program is growing---the two newest cohorts (2024-2025 and 2025-2026) together make up 64% of enrolled students.
About 72% of students have a WAG of 2.25 or better, indicating solid overall academic performance. The majority cluster in the 1.51-2.00 range.
The oldest cohort (21-22) has the best WAG (1.657) and is near completion. The high rate of 5.00 grades across middle cohorts (59%) is primarily driven by Math 21.
36 students (13.4%) are near or at completion (120+ credited units)
57 students (21.2%) are in their early stages (<30 units) - consistent with the large incoming cohort
It is expected that almost all students at this point have already completed HRIM 110 (Macro Perspectives), as it is offered every first semester.

Almost 5% of the students have yet to pass HRIM 116 Introduction to Accounting, showing as an early sign of a bottleneck. However, HRIM 116 is offered both semesters to cater to non-HRIM students during 2nd semester.
More students have passed Stat 101 than Math 21, given that for non-STEM graduates, they are also required to pass a non-credit course Math 20.
The low completion rates for upper-level courses (HRIM 150+) are expected---these are taken in the later years of the program, and many students are still in their first or second year.

PI 100 appears to be frequently deferred, even among older cohorts. As the whole university is required to take this course, limited slots become available. In the curriculum, the students are advised to take the course during the midyear after their third year. The students in the younger cohorts who have already taken the course are either transferees from another UP Campus, or shiftees from another program within UP Diliman.
Math 21 is the single most problematic course in the curriculum:
84 students (31%) have recorded 5.0 (failing) grade in Math 21
83 students (31%) had to repeat Math 21 at least once
This represents a significant disruption to normal progression, as Math 21, along with Stat 101, is a prerequisite to HRIM 131, which is also the gateway to HRIM 150 series.
67 students (24.9%) have at least one INC grade on record.
140 students (52%) have at least one DRP (dropped course) on record
High DRP rates in Math 21 suggest students are strategically withdrawing to avoid failing.
Students with WAG <= 1.50 and at least 60 credited units (2nd year and above)

Math 21 is a critical pain point. Nearly 1 in 3 students has failed it at least once, and over half of all students have a DRP on their record (largely from Math 21). Targeted support (tutorials, bridging programs) could significantly improve throughput.
Overall academic health is good. The average WAG of 1.81 is strong. About 72% of students are at 2.25 or better.
36 students are near graduation (120+ units). Most are from the 21-22 and 22-23 cohorts and have WAGs in the 1.35-1.97 range.
